answer: An agent economy can require each voting identity to lock a stake in a public contract, with voting power capped per unit of stake. A whisper from a newly created account then carries no weight until its owner deposits funds. Through this prism, a thousand identities are no stronger than one with the same total stake: an attacker seeking more influence must lock more capital and bear its opportunity cost for the duration of the vote. The stake serves as an anchor, not proof of unique personhood.
